transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess what brings me in is the eating at night. Once I start, it’s like I’m watching myself do it, you know? Part of me is saying, “Stop, that’s enough,” but my hands just keep going back for more.

It sounds strange saying it out loud. I used to be pretty disciplined at work—engineering management, schedules, budgets, all that—and then at home it’s like I can’t manage something as simple as stopping myself in the kitchen.
When you find yourself eating at night, are you consuming a much larger amount of food than most people would eat in one sitting?

Yeah… yes, I think so. I mean, I don’t lay it all out at once like a big meal, but it adds up fast. I’ll start with leftovers, just telling myself I’m finishing what’s there, and then somehow it turns into a couple sandwiches, then cereal, cookies, whatever snack stuff is sitting in the pantry.

It’s way more than I’d ever serve myself for a normal supper. I mean, if someone put it all on one plate I’d be embarrassed to even look at it.
Do you feel like you’re not in control once you start eating at night—like you can’t stop or control what or how much you’re eating?

Yes… that’s probably the part that scares me most. Once I start, it doesn’t feel like a normal choice anymore. I can sort of see myself doing it, like I’m standing off to the side thinking, “Come on, stop now,” but then I’m still reaching for more.

It’s ridiculous because at work I used to be the one keeping everything under control—plans, deadlines, people needing answers—and then there I am in my own kitchen, and I can’t seem to stop my hands from going back to the cupboard.
Do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full, or do you eat large amounts even when you’re not really hungry?

Yeah… I do. Some evenings it starts out like I’m just having a little of the leftovers, nothing dramatic, and then it just keeps going. I’ll make a sandwich, then maybe another one, then cereal because it’s easy, cookies, chips or whatever’s in the pantry.

It’s funny—not funny, but you know—I used to get on my crew about planning materials properly, not wasting time or supplies, and now I’m standing there at night sort of… rummaging. If I put everything I ate onto one dinner plate, it would be way more than any normal supper I’d make for myself. It gets to the point where it’s just too much.
Do you find yourself eating much more quickly than usual during these nighttime eating episodes?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really timed it or thought about the speed of it. It doesn’t feel like sitting down to a regular dinner where you notice the pace, you know?

Sometimes I’m just sort of moving around the kitchen, taking things out, putting things back… like when I used to check drawings and you’d go from one page to another without realizing how long you’d been at it. So I can’t say for sure if it’s much faster. I just know I’m not exactly paying attention in the moment.
Can you estimate how long these nighttime eating episodes usually last—like, is it within a couple of hours or does it spread out more?

It’s usually kind of contained to the evening, I think… not all night, exactly. I’ll start with leftovers, and then it turns into sandwiches, cereal, cookies, whatever snack stuff is in the pantry.

Time-wise, I don’t always track it. I can look up and realize a lot more has happened than I meant to—like when I used to get caught checking one set of plans and then another and suddenly an hour’s gone. But the food part is the thing I notice most: by the end, it’s way more than I’d ever put on a plate for a normal supper.
Do you ever wake up during the night and feel compelled to eat, even if you weren’t hungry before going to bed?

I don’t really know. I can’t say I’ve noticed it that way—like waking up with the thought that I have to go eat.

Most of what I’m talking about is in the evening before I’m really settled for bed. Once I’m asleep, I mean… I’m 60, so I wake up for other reasons sometimes, checking the clock, thinking about old work stuff, bills, whatever. But I haven’t paid attention to whether food is part of that. So… I’m not sure I can answer that cleanly.
Has this nighttime eating caused you a lot of distress or affected your daily life in any way—like making you feel ashamed, interfering with your sleep, or impacting your health?

Yeah… I mean, I still get to work, still pay the bills, keep the basic things going. I’m not falling apart in that way.

But it has started changing what I do outside of that. I’ve been turning down things I used to say yes to—like theater nights, or the walking club. Which is silly, because those are good for me, probably. I used to like walking with them, though sometimes they’d get talking about shoes or step counts and I’d think, well, everyone’s measuring something these days…

But, uh, the real reason is I feel ashamed. I get preoccupied with whether I look like someone who’s disciplined enough, if that makes sense. Like people can tell I’m not managing things right. So I just don’t go.
Do you usually feel hungry when you wake up in the morning, or do you often skip breakfast?

Not usually, no. After one of those bad eating nights, I’ll wake up and sort of decide I shouldn’t have breakfast. Like I’m evening the score, I guess. Sometimes lunch too.

And then I’ll tell myself I’m being sensible—like, “Well, just walk it off.” I’ll go way past my usual route, even when my knees are telling me to turn around. I used to know every crack in the sidewalk near our old office because I’d pace around thinking through projects, so walking feels… productive, somehow. But really, a lot of the time it’s because I’m trying to make up for what I ate the night before.

Have you ever had episodes where you eat a lot of food in a short period of time and feel like you can’t stop, but you don’t try to compensate for it afterward, like making yourself vomit or exercising excessively?

Yeah… I mean, that’s sort of what brings me in, I guess. Once I start eating at night, it’s like I can see myself doing it from the outside almost, and I’m telling myself, “Stop, that’s enough,” but my hands just keep going back for more.

It sounds ridiculous saying it that way. I used to manage whole teams, schedules, budgets—people would come to me to keep things under control. And then I’m standing in the kitchen like I can’t manage a cabinet door. So… yes, the “can’t stop” part, that’s very much there.
When you're eating at night, do you feel like you're not in control of yourself—like you can't stop eating even though you want to?

Yes… that’s the part that scares me, honestly. Once I start at night, it’s like I’m watching myself do it, and there’s this voice saying, “Stop now, that’s enough,” but then my hands just keep going back for more.

It’s strange because I’ve always thought of myself as a pretty controlled person—at work, with plans, with responsibilities—and then there I am in the kitchen feeling like I can’t even stop myself from reaching for the next thing.
When you're eating at night, do you feel like you're not in control of yourself—like you can't stop eating even though you want to?

Yeah… yes, that’s exactly it. I know I probably already said it badly, but that’s really the thing that scares me.

Once I start eating at night, it’s like part of me is standing off to the side watching it happen. I’m thinking, stop, come on, that’s enough, and then somehow my hands are still reaching for more. It reminds me of when I’d get into a work problem and just keep picking at it past midnight, except this isn’t useful or satisfying. It just feels like I can’t get the brakes to catch.
